name: Saint Charbel Makhlouf
history: A Maronite monk and priest of Lebanon who spent his last twenty-three years as a hermit, in prayer, fasting and manual work, celebrating Mass with great devotion. After his death light was reported around his grave and his body was found incorrupt. Thousands of healings have been attributed to him. Paul VI canonised him in 1977.
life: Youssef Antoun Makhlouf was born in the mountain village of Bekaa Kafra, in northern Lebanon, and lost his father when he was three. Raised by his mother and devout uncles, two of whom were hermits, he left home at twenty-three to enter the Lebanese Maronite Order, taking the name Charbel after an early martyr. He was ordained priest in 1859 and lived at the monastery of Saint Maron at Annaya for sixteen years. In 1875 he was allowed to withdraw to the hermitage of Saints Peter and Paul above the monastery, where he prayed, worked the land, ate once a day and spoke little. Each day he offered Mass with deep recollection. In December 1898 he suffered a stroke while celebrating Mass and died on Christmas Eve. His tomb at Annaya draws pilgrims of every faith, Christian and Muslim alike.
prayerTo: Saint Charbel, hermit of Lebanon, you left everything to live hidden with God, and He has made your hiddenness a light to many. Pray for Lebanon and the Christians of the Middle East, for the sick who come to you, and for me, that I may find God in silence and in the Mass. Amen.
penance: Eat simply today, keeping to one main meal if your health allows, and pray for peace in Lebanon and the Middle East.
meditation: He hardly spoke, and yet he still draws the world to God. What would God say through your silence?
